question: An air brake system is actually made up of three different braking systems working together. Which three?
choice_a: Foot brake, hand brake, and trailer brake
choice_b: Service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake
choice_c: Foundation brake, spring brake, and hydraulic brake
choice_d: Primary brake, secondary brake, and ABS brake
explanation: Air brakes are really three different braking systems: the service brake applies and releases the brakes during normal driving, the parking brake applies and releases the parking brakes, and the emergency brake uses parts of the service and parking systems to stop the vehicle if the brake system fails.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 62

question: About what tank pressure causes the air compressor governor to stop (cut out) the compressor from pumping air, and about what pressure allows it to start (cut in) again?
choice_a: Cut out around 150 psi, cut in around 125 psi
choice_b: Cut out around 125 psi, cut in around 100 psi
choice_c: Cut out around 100 psi, cut in around 80 psi
choice_d: Cut out around 90 psi, cut in around 55 psi
explanation: The governor stops the compressor from pumping air when tank pressure rises to the cut-out level, around 125 psi, and allows the compressor to start pumping again when pressure falls to the cut-in pressure, around 100 psi.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 62

question: Water and compressor oil collect in the bottom of an air tank and must be removed through a drain valve. How do manually operated drain valves differ from automatic ones?
choice_a: Manual valves only exist on trailers, while automatic valves only exist on tractors
choice_b: Manual valves are opened with a quarter turn or by pulling a cable and must be drained by the driver at the end of each day, while automatic valves expel water and oil on their own
choice_c: Manual valves remove oil only, while automatic valves remove water only
choice_d: Manual valves drain continuously while driving, while automatic valves only work when parked
explanation: Air tank drain valves are either manually operated, opened by a quarter turn or by pulling a cable and drained by the driver at the end of each day of driving, or automatic, which expel the water and oil on their own; automatic tanks can also be manually drained and may have electric heating devices to help prevent freezing.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 62

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator found on some air brake systems?
choice_a: To put alcohol into the air system, reducing the risk of ice forming in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather
choice_b: To cool the compressed air before it reaches the brake chambers
choice_c: To clean oil residue out of the air tanks
choice_d: To lubricate the air compressor
explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that puts alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather, since ice inside the system can make the brakes stop working; the container should be checked and filled daily during cold weather.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 62

question: A safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to. At about what pressure is it usually set to open?
choice_a: 150 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 125 psi
choice_d: 175 psi
explanation: The safety valve protects the tank and the rest of the system from too much pressure and is usually set to open at 150 psi; if the safety valve releases air, something is wrong and the fault should be fixed by a mechanic.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 62

question: The brake pedal on an air brake vehicle is also called the foot valve or treadle valve. What happens when the driver presses it down harder versus lets up on it?
choice_a: Pressing harder applies more air pressure; letting up reduces air pressure and releases the brakes, which lets air out of the system that the compressor must replace
choice_b: Pressing harder has no effect on pressure, only on pedal travel
choice_c: Pressing the pedal recharges the air tanks directly
choice_d: Letting up increases air pressure to the brakes
explanation: Pushing the pedal down harder applies more air pressure, while letting up reduces pressure and releases the brakes; releasing lets compressed air escape the system, so pressure in the tanks drops and must be made up by the compressor, which is why pressing and releasing the pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: In the most common type of foundation brake, the s-cam drum brake, what actually forces the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum?
choice_a: Hydraulic fluid pressing on the shoes
choice_b: The s-cam, twisted by the camshaft as the slack adjuster moves, which forces the shoes apart against the drum
choice_c: A power screw turned by the slack adjuster
choice_d: A wedge pushed directly between the ends of the brake shoes
explanation: When the brake pedal is pushed, air pressure moves the slack adjuster and twists the camshaft, turning the s-shaped cam; the s-cam forces the brake shoes away from one another and presses them against the inside of the brake drum, and a return spring pulls the shoes away when the pedal is released.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: How does a wedge-type foundation brake apply the brake shoes to the drum?
choice_a: Air pressure rotates an s-cam against the shoes
choice_b: A spring-loaded modulating valve forces the shoes outward
choice_c: The brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the inside of the drum
choice_d: A power screw clamps the shoes against the drum like a c-clamp
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the inside of the brake drum; wedge brakes may use a single chamber or two chambers, and may be self-adjusting or require manual adjustment.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: In air-operated disc brakes, what does the power screw do once the brake chamber and slack adjuster turn it?
choice_a: It forces alcohol into the evaporator
choice_b: It twists the s-cam against the brake shoes
choice_c: It opens the safety relief valve to release excess pressure
choice_d: It clamps the disc or rotor between the brake lining pads of a caliper, similar to a large c-clamp
explanation: In air-operated disc brakes, air pressure acts on a brake chamber and slack adjuster like s-cam brakes, but instead of an s-cam a power screw is used; the power screw clamps the disc or rotor between the brake lining pads of a caliper, similar to a large c-clamp. Wedge and disc brakes are less common than s-cam brakes.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: A vehicle's application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. What does it mean if the driver needs increasing application pressure just to hold the same speed?
choice_a: The brakes are fading, and the driver should slow down and use a lower gear
choice_b: The tractor protection valve has closed
choice_c: The alcohol evaporator needs refilling
choice_d: ABS has taken over braking control
explanation: Increasing application pressure needed to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading, and the driver should slow down and use a lower gear; the need for increased pressure can also be caused by brakes out of adjustment, air leaks, or mechanical problems.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: A low air pressure warning signal is required on vehicles with air brakes. Before the tank pressure falls below what level must a visible warning signal come on?
choice_a: 65 psi
choice_b: 45 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 75 psi
explanation: A warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 55 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles); the warning is usually a red light and may include a buzzer.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: How does an automatic 'wig wag' low air pressure warning device behave?
choice_a: It permanently disables the accelerator until pressure is restored
choice_b: It sounds only a buzzer with no visual signal
choice_c: It only functions once the vehicle exceeds 40 mph
choice_d: It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when pressure falls below 55 psi and rises out of view once pressure climbs back above 55 psi
explanation: The wig wag drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when the system pressure drops below 55 psi; an automatic wig wag rises back out of view once pressure in the system goes above 55 psi, while a manual reset type must be repositioned by the driver and will not stay out of view until pressure is restored.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: On large buses, it is common for the low air pressure warning devices to signal at what pressure range, rather than the standard 55 psi threshold used on most vehicles?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi, higher than the general 55 psi requirement for other air brake vehicles.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 63

question: Why do trucks, truck-tractors, and buses rely on spring brakes (mechanical force) to hold the emergency and parking brakes on, rather than air pressure alone?
choice_a: Because spring brakes stop the vehicle faster than service brakes
choice_b: Because springs create less wear on brake linings than air pressure
choice_c: Because air pressure can eventually leak away, so a mechanical hold is required to keep the brakes applied
choice_d: Because federal law requires an electric backup system instead
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet this need, held back by air pressure while driving, with the springs applying the brakes if air pressure is removed or lost through a leak.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 64

question: On a tractor or straight truck, spring brakes come fully on automatically once air pressure drops into what range?
choice_a: 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi)
choice_b: 5 to 15 psi
choice_c: 70 to 90 psi
choice_d: 50 to 65 psi
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi; drivers should not wait for this and should bring the vehicle to a safe stop as soon as the low air pressure warning first activates.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 64

question: On newer air brake vehicles, what does the driver use to apply and release the parking (spring) brakes?
choice_a: The same handle used for the modulating control valve on older vehicles
choice_b: A diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob, pulled out to apply and pushed in to release
choice_c: A round red foot pedal beside the treadle valve
choice_d: A rocker switch on the dashboard labeled ABS
explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the driver puts on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob, pulling it out to apply the spring brakes and pushing it in to release them; older vehicles may use a lever instead.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 64

question: Why does the manual caution drivers never to push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are already applied?
choice_a: It will automatically release the parking brake knob
choice_b: The combined force of the springs and the air pressure could damage the brakes
choice_c: It triggers the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_d: It has no effect since the pedal is mechanically locked out
explanation: Pushing the brake pedal down while the spring brakes are on could damage the brakes from the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure; many systems are designed to prevent this, but not all are, so drivers should develop the habit of not doing it.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 64

question: Under the manual's date requirements, truck-tractors with air brakes built on or after what date must be equipped with antilock brakes?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: January 1, 1994
choice_c: January 1, 2000
choice_d: March 1, 1998
explanation: Truck-tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to have ABS, while other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) are required to have it if built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 65

question: Where are the required yellow ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers?
choice_a: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_b: Underneath the trailer near the kingpin
choice_c: Centered on the rear bumper
choice_d: On the instrument panel inside the cab
explanation: Trailers have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner, while tractors, trucks, and buses carry their malfunction lamps on the instrument panel; dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 are also required to have one.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 65

question: According to the manual, how does ABS change a vehicle's normal braking capability?
choice_a: It replaces the need for spring brakes entirely
choice_b: It decreases stopping power slightly to prevent wheel lockup
choice_c: It does not decrease or increase normal braking capability; it only activates when wheels are about to lock up
choice_d: It increases stopping power on every stop
explanation: ABS is an addition to normal brakes and does not decrease or increase normal braking capability; it only activates when wheels are about to lock up, and while it does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, it helps keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 65

question: What defines a dual air brake system, which most heavy-duty vehicles use for safety?
choice_a: Two separate brake pedals the driver alternates between
choice_b: A single air system with two alcohol evaporators for redundancy
choice_c: Two completely separate air brake systems, each with its own tanks, hoses, and lines, operated with a single set of brake controls
choice_d: One air system paired with a hydraulic backup system
explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems using a single set of brake controls; each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. The primary system typically operates the rear axle brakes and the secondary system operates the front axle brakes, and both supply air to a trailer if there is one.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 66

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should allow the compressor to build up at least how much pressure in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 55 psi
choice_b: 80 psi
choice_c: 125 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, the driver should allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems, watching both gauges as pressure rises.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 66

question: During a walk-around inspection, after releasing the parking brakes and pulling hard on a slack adjuster, how much movement at the push rod connection indicates it probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: Movement of more than about one foot
choice_b: Any movement at all, however slight
choice_c: Movement of more than about one inch
choice_d: Movement of more than about six inches
explanation: After parking on level ground, chocking the wheels, and releasing the parking brakes, if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment; out-of-adjustment brakes are the most common problem found in roadside inspections.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 66

question: During an air brake inspection, what is the limit on cracks found in a brake drum or disc?
choice_a: Cracks only matter if the vehicle also has worn linings
choice_b: Cracks are acceptable up to the full width of the friction area
choice_c: Cracks are acceptable as long as they are not longer than one half the width of the friction area
choice_d: No cracks of any length are permitted
explanation: Brake drums or discs must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area; linings must not be loose, soaked with oil or grease, or dangerously thin, and mechanical parts must not be broken or missing.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 67

question: During the final air brake check, with the air system fully charged and the engine shut off, how much pressure drop over one minute is acceptable before it is considered too much air loss?
choice_a: No more than 1 psi (single) or 2 psi (combination)
choice_b: No more than 10 psi for any vehicle type
choice_c: No more than 5 psi (single) or 6 psi (combination)
choice_d: No more than 3 psi (single) or 4 psi (combination)
explanation: After the air gauges stabilize and the foot brake is held for one minute, the air loss rate is too much if pressure drops more than three psi in one minute for a single vehicle, or more than four psi in one minute for a combination vehicle; if it falls faster, the driver should check for leaks and fix them before driving.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 67

question: Which emergency stopping method involves applying the brakes all the way, releasing them as soon as the wheels lock up, and reapplying them fully once the wheels start rolling again?
choice_a: Modulated braking
choice_b: Stab braking
choice_c: Controlled braking
choice_d: Threshold braking
explanation: Stab braking means applying the brakes all the way, releasing them when the wheels lock up, and applying them fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling; it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after release, and reapplying too soon will keep the vehicle from straightening out.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 68

question: In the 'controlled braking' emergency stopping method, how does the driver apply the brakes?
choice_a: By fully releasing the brakes the moment any wheel begins to slow
choice_b: Only lightly, to avoid triggering the spring brakes
choice_c: By pumping the pedal rapidly and continuously regardless of wheel lockup
choice_d: As hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small
explanation: With controlled braking, the driver applies the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels while keeping steering wheel movements very small; if a larger steering adjustment is needed or the wheels lock, the driver releases the brakes and reapplies as soon as possible.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 68

question: Air brakes take extra time to work compared to hydraulic brakes because of 'brake lag.' About how much extra distance does brake lag add at 55 mph on dry pavement, and how far is the total stopping distance under good conditions at that speed?
choice_a: About 32 feet of lag, total stopping distance over 450 feet
choice_b: About 10 feet of lag, total stopping distance around 250 feet
choice_c: About 100 feet of lag, total stopping distance over 800 feet
choice_d: About 60 feet of lag, total stopping distance over 600 feet
explanation: Unlike hydraulic brakes, which work almost instantly, air brakes take a little time (one half second or more) for the air to flow through the lines to the brakes; this brake lag adds about 32 feet of distance at 55 mph on dry pavement, making the total stopping distance for an average driver over 450 feet under good traction and brake conditions.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 69

question: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving, what should the driver do, and why can a heavily loaded vehicle take a long distance to stop once spring brakes engage?
choice_a: Immediately shift into the highest gear to reduce engine strain
choice_b: Ignore the warning until the wig wag arm physically drops into view
choice_c: Stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible, because a heavily loaded vehicle takes a long distance to stop since the spring brakes do not work on all axles
choice_d: Continue driving normally since spring brakes provide full stopping power at every axle
explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, the driver should stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible since there might be an air leak; controlled braking is only possible while enough air remains, and a heavily loaded vehicle takes a long distance to stop once the spring brakes come on because they do not work on all axles.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 70
